v.en: O God, come to my assistance;

r.la: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
r.en: And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

full.en: God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.

la: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
en: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

v.la: Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam.
v.en: To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness.

r.en: And the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

text.en: Our God * is our helper in troubles.

text.la: Magnus Dóminus * et laudábilis nimis in civitáte Dei nostri. ‡
text.en: Great is the Lord * and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God. ‡

text.la: Os meum loquétur * sapiéntiam: et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
text.en: My mouth shall speak * wisdom: and the meditation of my heart understanding.

text.la: Ne timúeris * cum dívite non descéndet in sepúlcrum glória eius.
text.en: Be not thou afraid * the things which made him rich, or his glory shall not descend with him to the sepulchre.
The God of gods, * the Lord hath spoken. ‡
Understand these things, * you that forget God.

text.la: Acceptábis sacrifícium * iustítiæ super altáre tuum, Dómine.
text.en: Thou shalt accept the sacrifice * of justice, upon thy altar, O Lord.

text.la: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
text.en: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

text.la: A vínculis peccatórum nostrórum absólvat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.
text.en: May the Almighty and merciful Lord loose us from the bonds of our sins.

benedictio.la: Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
benedictio.en: May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.

source.en: Lesson from the second letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

text.la: 1 Has ergo habéntes promissiónes, caríssimi, mundémus nos ab omni inquinaménto carnis et spíritus, perficiéntes sanctificatiónem in timóre Dei. 2 Cápite nos. Néminem lǽsimus, néminem corrúpimus, néminem circumvénimus. 3 Non ad condemnatiónem vestram dico. Prædíximus enim, quod in córdibus nostris estis ad commoriéndum, et ad convivéndum.
text.en: 1 Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God. 2 Receive us. We have injured no man, we have corrupted no man, we have overreached no man. 3 I speak not this to your condemnation. For we have said before, that you are in our hearts, to die together, and to live together.

body.la: Ne perdíderis me cum iniquitátibus meis:
body.en: Cut me not off in the midst of my sins.

refrain.la: Neque in finem irátus resérves mala mea.
refrain.en: Nor keep thy wrath against me for my latter end.

verse.la: Non intres in iudícium cum servo tuo, Dómine.
verse.en: Enter not into judgment with thy servant, O Lord.

benedictio.en: God's most mighty strength alway be His people's staff and stay.

text.la: 4 Multa mihi fidúcia est apud vos, multa mihi gloriátio pro vobis, replétus sum consolatióne, superabúndo gáudio in omni tribulatióne nostra. 5 Nam et cum venissémus in Macedóniam, nullam réquiem hábuit caro nostra, sed omnem tribulatiónem passi sumus: foris pugnæ, intus timóres. 6 Sed qui consolátur húmiles, consolátus est nos Deus in advéntu Titi. 7 Non solum autem in advéntu eius, sed étiam in consolatióne, qua consolátus est in vobis, réferens nobis vestrum desidérium, vestrum fletum, vestram æmulatiónem pro me, ita ut magis gaudérem.
text.en: 4 Great is my confidence for you, great is my glorying for you. I am filled with comfort: I exceedingly abound with joy in all our tribulation. 5 For also when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we suffered all tribulation; combats without, fears within. 6 But God, who comforteth the humble, comforted us by the coming of Titus. 7 And not by his coming only, but also by the consolation, wherewith he was comforted in you, relating to us your desire, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced the more.

body.la: Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum:
body.en: My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready.

refrain.en: I will sing and give praise to the Lord.

verse.la: Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara, exsúrgam dilúculo.
verse.en: Awake up, my glory, awake, psaltery and harp! I will awake early.

benedictio.la: Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.
benedictio.en: May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.

text.la: 8 Quóniam etsi contristávi vos in epístola, non me pœ́nitet: et si pœnitéret, videns quod epístola illa vos contristávit; 9 Nunc gáudeo: non quia contristáti estis, sed quia contristáti estis ad pœniténtiam. Contristáti enim estis secúndum Deum, ut in nullo detriméntum patiámini ex nobis. 10 Quæ enim secúndum Deum tristítia est, pœniténtiam in salútem stábilem operátur: sǽculi autem tristítia mortem operátur.
text.en: 8 For although I made you sorrowful by my epistle, I do not repent; and if I did repent, seeing that the same epistle did make you sorrowful; 9 Now I am glad: not because you were made sorrowful; but because you were made sorrowful unto penance. For you were made sorrowful according to God, that you might suffer damage by us in nothing. 10 For the sorrow that is according to God worketh penance, steadfast unto salvation; but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

body.la: Adiútor meus, tibi psallam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es:
body.en: Unto thee, O my Strength, will I sing, for God is my defence,

verse.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
verse.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

text.la: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi Laudes separandæ sint.
text.en: Skip the rest, unless praying Lauds separately.

text.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui cæléstia simul et terréna moderáris: supplicatiónes pópuli tui cleménter exáudi; et pacem tuam nostris concéde tempóribus.
text.en: Almighty and eternal God, as thou govern all things in heaven and on earth; in thy mercy hear the supplication of thy people, and grant thy peace in our times.

office.title: Feria IV infra Hebd II post Epiphaniam
